conventions.convention: The spaces are real Hilbert spaces. A weakly closed forward map has a nonempty topologically weakly closed domain and a sequentially weak-to-weak closed graph; weak-to-strong graph closure alone is not the stipulated condition.
J(x) = ||F(x)-y||²/2 + α||x-x0||²/2 is defined on D for α > 0 and x0 ∈ X. Minimizers are global over D; existence and uniqueness are not part of the definition.
An x0-minimum-norm solution minimizes distance to the specified x0 over all exact solutions in D, with no uniqueness assertion.
Existence and compactness results assume the ultrafilter lemma, dependent choice, and real HB. DC supplies the countable choice used for selections and Hilbert reflexivity.

Vanishing-noise convergence assumes exact solvability, δn ≥ 0 tending to zero, αn > 0 tending to zero, δn²/αn tending to zero, and ||yn-y†|| ≤ δn. Its stated conclusion concerns weak subsequential limits, without uniqueness or full-sequence convergence.

load_bearing.statement: We call F a weakly closed forward map when its domain is weakly closed and its graph is sequentially weak-to-weak closed.

Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, DC, and real HB, for real Hilbert spaces X,Y and a weakly closed forward map F:D→Y, Jα,y,x0 attains a global minimum on D for every α>0, x0∈X, and y∈Y. No exact solution of F(x)=y is required.
For real Hilbert spaces X,Y, a nonempty D⊆X, F:D→Y, α>0, x0∈X, and y∈Y, Jα,y,x0(x) := ||F(x)-y||²/2 + α||x-x0||²/2 for x∈D.
For a weakly closed forward map F:D→Y between real Hilbert spaces and y∈Y, SF(y):={x∈D:F(x)=y} is weakly sequentially closed in X.

Assuming the ultrafilter lemma, DC, and HB, a weakly closed forward map F:D→Y between real Hilbert spaces with nonempty SF(y) has, for every x0∈X, an exact solution x† whose distance to x0 is no greater than that of any other exact solution in D.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite's nonlinear-forward-map and minimum-distance definitions use nonempty norm-open domains. The assigned batch explicitly introduces its separate weakly closed-domain interface, retains the same global reference-distance meaning, and does not infer weak graph closure from differentiability or tangential cone control.

The rate theorem's F7 and Hilbert specialization use exactly the quadratic Tikhonov functional. The specialization expressly assumes a supplied global minimizer and does not claim existence on its open domain from this batch's weakly closed-domain theorem.

The page retains this prerequisite, but its items contain no direct citation to an assigned batch-26 item. The model contract and algorithm cite the quadratic objective with matching residual, reference point, positive parameter, and admissible domain.
